rawCandidates.title: Deep-maintenance chat command deletes generated task notes without authorization, confirmation, or audit
rawCandidates.source: Any chat user able to invoke /plur1bus can request obsidian maintenance deep; the common Obsidian command dispatch does not enforce configured PLUR1BUS allowlists.
rawCandidates.control: runLivingMaintenanceDeep is called directly at lib/obsidian-control-room.js:3444, with no dry-run flag, user/chat-bound confirmation nonce, or checkAuth; index.js:2948-2983 reaches it before destructive authorization branches.
rawCandidates.sink: cleanupResolvedFindings unconditionally enumerates records/tasks and calls unlinkSync for every missing-<field>-<id>.md whose source ID is no longer classified as missing at lib/obsidian/maintenance-deep.js:31-39.
rawCandidates.impact: An unauthorized shared-chat participant can remove generated review findings/evidence and alter the human control-room state despite an allowlist; deletions have no archive or appendDestructiveOpLog receipt.
rawCandidates.validationFacts: Static reachability is direct. Validation should invoke the registered command handler as a user excluded by allowedUserIds against a temporary contained review root with a matching stale missing-field task, and verify that the file is removed while no confirmation or destructive audit callback is consulted.
rawCandidates.attackFacts: Preconditions are chat command access, at least one generated missing-field task whose source no longer appears missing, and write access to the review vault. File-name matching and the fixed contained tasks directory limit scope. A feature-preserving fix is to retain automatic cleanup but place its mutating phase behind existing authorization, preview/confirmation, archival, and audit-log primitives.

notes: One destructive command candidate. Non-mutating maintenance analysis should remain available; only the cleanup mutation needs the existing authorization/confirmation/audit boundary.
